# Set-up

First, all necessary libraries are imported, the data is read in, and all necessary variables are produced.

```{r set_up, message=FALSE}
# First, the libraries 
# If you want to replicate my environment exactly, use renv::restore()
library(tidyverse)
library(mediation)
library(lavaan)
library(multcomp)
library(knitr)
select = dplyr::select

# Next, reading the data
GLAB = c("Mindset", "Education", "No-intervention")
df = read.csv("../deidentified_data.csv") %>%
  mutate(group = recode_values(t2_Group.ID, from = c(1, 2, 3),
                               to = GLAB), # Group names
         female = case_when(t1_sex == 1 ~ 1,
                            t1_sex == 0 ~ 0,
                            TRUE ~ NA), # Recode sex
         chg_PEM_avg = t2_PEM_avg - t1_PEM_avg, # Change scores
         t3_OAcomp = t3_IMI_man + t3_IMI_opp - t3_IMI_cat,
         t2_OAcomp = t2_IMI_man + t2_IMI_opp - t2_IMI_cat,
         t1_OAcomp = t1_IMI_man + t1_IMI_opp - t1_IMI_cat,
         Y_surgery = t3_surgery - t1_surgery,
         Y_limit = case_when(t1_management_11 - t3_management_11 > 0 ~ 1,
                             TRUE ~ 0), # Only improvement is a "1"
         Y_inject = case_when(t1_management_2 - t3_management_2 > 0 ~ 1,
                              TRUE ~ 0),
         Y_TSK = t3_TSK_avg - t1_TSK_avg,
         Y_ASEp = t3_ASE_pain_avg - t1_ASE_pain_avg,
         chg_OAcomp = t2_OAcomp - t1_OAcomp, # Baseline features
         bilateral = case_when(t1_uni.bi == 5 ~ 1,
                               t1_uni.bi == 4 ~ 0,
                               TRUE ~ NA),
         minority = case_when(!(t1_race %in% c("6", "")) ~ 1,
                              TRUE ~ 0),
         employed = case_when(grepl("[1-2]", t1_employment) ~ 1,
                              TRUE ~ 0),
         depression = case_when(grepl("10", t1_med.cond) ~ 1, 
                                TRUE ~ 0),
         n_comorbid = lengths(strsplit(t1_med.cond, ",")),
         Y_pase = t3_PASE_total - t1_PASE_total) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = GLAB[c(3,2,1)]))
```

# Analysis 1 - Moderators of the Treatment Effect

## Unadjusted Moderation Analyses

For the first set of moderation analysis, we regress exercise mindset at time point 2 onto baseline exercise mindset and the interaction between the intervention group and a chosen potential moderator. Models are fit for each potential moderator independently, extracting the corresponding interaction estimates and p-values. We leverage linear regression throughout for simplicity, as no boundary effects were observed. For this set of models, we do not adjust for confounders, instead relying upon the randomization from the original trial. We will assess the impact of adjusting for confounders later.

```{r moderation_models}
# Variables of interest
demo_vars = c("female", "minority", "employed", "t1_age")
health_status = c("bilateral", "t1_bmi", "n_comorbid", "t1_pain", "t1_pain.time",
                  "t1_ASE_pain_avg", "t1_TSK_avg", "t1_PASE_total")
names(demo_vars) = c("Female", "Racial/ethnic minority", "Employed", "Age")
names(health_status) = c("Bilateral symptoms", "BMI", "# comorbidities",  
                         "Baseline Pain", "Symptom duration", "Baseline self-efficacy",
                         "Baseline fear of movement", "Baseline activity")

# Standardize continuous variables, convert binary to factor
bin_vars = c(demo_vars[1:3], health_status[1])
cont_vars = c(demo_vars[4], health_status[-c(1)])
for_mod = df %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(cont_vars), ~ scale(.x)[,1]),
         across(all_of(bin_vars), ~ factor(.x))) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Mindset", "Education", "No-intervention")))

# Map over demographic variables and fit models
demo_fits = imap(demo_vars, function(x, y){
  # Model formula
  form = as.formula(paste0("t2_PEM_avg ~ t1_PEM_avg + group*", x)) 
  
  # Fit OLS regression
  mod = lm(form, data = for_mod)
  
  # Extract coefficients and p-values
  coef_df = summary(mod)$coefficients
  n_ests = nrow(coef_df)
  
  # Estimands are in the last two rows
  return(data.frame(Var = y, 
                    Comparator = c("Education", "None"),
                    p_value = coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 4],
                    interaction = -coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 1]))
}) %>% list_rbind()

# Map over health status variables and fit models
health_fits = imap(health_status, function(x, y){
  # Model formula
  form = as.formula(paste0("t2_PEM_avg ~ t1_PEM_avg + group*", x)) 
  
  # Fit OLS regression
  mod = lm(form, data = for_mod) 
  
  # Extract coefficients and p-values
  coef_df = summary(mod)$coefficients 
  n_ests = nrow(coef_df)
  
  # Estimands are in the last two rows
  return(data.frame(Var = y, 
                    Comparator = c("Education", "None"),
                    p_value = coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 4],
                    interaction = -coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 1]))
}) %>% list_rbind()
```

## Multiplicity Adjustment

We next adjust the p-values to account for multiple testing using Benjamini Hochberg and Bonferroni correction. Here, we collect the moderators into two groups for the purposes of multiple testing, those which are related to demographic features (gender, minority status, age, employment) and those related to prior health status and function.

```{r moderation_pvals}
rbind(demo_fits, health_fits) %>%
  mutate(Grouping = case_when(Var %in% names(demo_vars) ~ "Demographics", 
                              TRUE ~ "Health Status")) %>%
  group_by(Grouping) %>%
  mutate(BH = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"), 
         Bonferroni = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni")) %>%
  arrange(p_value)
```

Under Benjamini-Hochberg correction, baseline self-efficacy, fear of movement, and pain are statistically significant moderators of the treatment effect on exercise mindset regardless of reference group. Baseline activity additionally moderates the relationship, but only when the comparator is the no-intervention arm. Almost all of these interactions are still significant under the more conservative Bonferroni correction, with the exception of baseline fear of movement and pain relative to the no intervention comparison group.

## Adjusted Moderation Analyses

We now adjust for several potential confounders as a sensitivity. We include depression status, baseline pain self efficacy, baseline other symptom self efficacy, and baseline OA mindset.

```{r adjusted_moderation}
# Map over demographic variables and fit models
demo_fits = imap(demo_vars, function(x, y){
  # Model formula
  form = as.formula(paste0("t2_PEM_avg ~ t1_PEM_avg + depression + t1_ASE_function_avg + t1_ASE_pain_avg + t1_OAcomp + group*", x)) 
  
  # Fit OLS regression
  mod = lm(form, data = for_mod)
  
  # Extract coefficients and p-values
  coef_df = summary(mod)$coefficients
  n_ests = nrow(coef_df)
  
  # Estimands are in the last two rows
  return(data.frame(Var = y, 
                    Comparator = c("Education", "None"),
                    p_value = coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 4],
                    interaction = -coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 1]))
}) %>% list_rbind()

# Map over health status variables and fit models
health_fits = imap(health_status, function(x, y){
  # Model formula
  form = as.formula(paste0("t2_PEM_avg ~ t1_PEM_avg + depression + t1_ASE_function_avg + t1_ASE_pain_avg + t1_OAcomp + group*", x)) 
  
  # Fit OLS regression
  mod = lm(form, data = for_mod) 
  
  # Extract coefficients and p-values
  coef_df = summary(mod)$coefficients 
  n_ests = nrow(coef_df)
  
  # Estimands are in the last two rows
  return(data.frame(Var = y, 
                    Comparator = c("Education", "None"),
                    p_value = coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 4],
                    interaction = -coef_df[c(n_ests-1, n_ests), 1]))
}) %>% list_rbind()

rbind(demo_fits, health_fits) %>%
  mutate(Grouping = case_when(Var %in% names(demo_vars) ~ "Demographics", 
                              TRUE ~ "Health Status")) %>%
  group_by(Grouping) %>%
  mutate(BH = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"), 
         Bonferroni = p.adjust(p_value, method = "bonferroni")) %>%
  arrange(p_value)
```

After confounder adjustment, results remain qualitatively similar. Baseline self-efficacy, fear of movement, and pain are statistically significant moderators of the treatment effect on exercise mindset regardless of reference group under Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment. Only baseline pain compared to the no intervention group is not still significant after the more conservative Bonferroni adjustment. Notably, baseline activity is not significant under any level of correction after incorporating confounders.

# Analysis 2 - Heterogeneity of Treatment Effects

We begin by defining a simple function of baseline knee pain (+), physical activity (-), and arthritis pain self-efficacy (-) which can be used as a suitability criterion. We examine estimated treatment effect within each strata of this criterion.

```{r strata_simple_tertiles}
# Filter to MINDSET vs NONE
suit_df = df %>%
  filter(t2_Group.ID %in% c(1, 3)) %>% 
  mutate(Treat = case_when(t2_Group.ID == 1 ~ "treat",
                           TRUE ~ "no"))

# Define the criterion
suit_df = suit_df %>%
  mutate(z_t1_pain = scale(t1_pain)[,1], # Z-score contributing features
         z_t1_PASE_total = scale(t1_PASE_total)[,1],
         z_t1_ASE_pain_avg = scale(t1_ASE_pain_avg)[,1],
         suitability = z_t1_pain - z_t1_PASE_total - z_t1_ASE_pain_avg)

# Stratify and examine ATE (mean difference due to RCT)
suit_df %>%
  mutate(tertile = ntile(suitability, 3), # Generate tertiles
         Strata = case_when(tertile == 1 ~ "Low",
                            tertile == 2 ~ "Mid",
                            tertile == 3 ~ "High"), 
         Strata = factor(Strata, levels = c("Low", "Mid", "High"))) %>%
  group_by(Strata, Treat) %>%  # Calculate average outcome within groups
  summarise(avg_SE = mean(Y_ASEp), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Treat, values_from = avg_SE) %>%
  mutate(ATE = treat - no) %>%
  select(-c(treat, no))
```

We can also examine the estimated treatment effects on self-efficacy within sub-populations chosen based upon thresholds for each of the contributing baseline features, giving an idea of the potential effects of enrollment rules. The assessed enrollment rules are: 1) baseline pain exceeds threshold; 2) baseline self efficacy below threshold; and 3) baseline activity below threshold. Thresholds are set to the population median for these assessments.

```{r strata_simple_enrollment}
ATE_est <- function(df){
  output = df %>%
    group_by(Treat) %>%
    summarise(avg_SE = mean(Y_ASEp)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Treat, values_from = avg_SE) %>%
    mutate(ATE = treat - no) %>%
    pull(ATE)
  return(output)
}

enroll_df = suit_df %>%
  mutate(pain_thresh = case_when(t1_pain >= median(t1_pain) ~ TRUE, TRUE ~ FALSE),
         selfeff_thresh = case_when(t1_ASE_pain_avg <= median(t1_ASE_pain_avg) ~ TRUE, 
                                    TRUE ~ FALSE), 
         activ_thresh = case_when(t1_PASE_total <= median(t1_PASE_total) ~ TRUE, 
                                  TRUE ~ FALSE))

highpain_lowselfeff = enroll_df %>%
  filter(pain_thresh & selfeff_thresh)
allthree = enroll_df %>%
  filter(pain_thresh & selfeff_thresh & activ_thresh)

data.frame(Enrollment_Rules = c("All Elligible", "High pain & low self-efficacy", "All three"), 
           Benefit = c(ATE_est(enroll_df),
                       ATE_est(highpain_lowselfeff),
                       ATE_est(allthree)),  
           Qualifying_Percent = 100 * c(1,
                                        nrow(highpain_lowselfeff) / nrow(enroll_df),
                                        nrow(allthree) / nrow(enroll_df)))
```

As an alternative to this fixed weighting, we can calculate the first principal component among these three baseline measures, which defines the axis of greatest variation among them for this population. Similar to the procedure used for the simple criterion, we can examine the estimated treatment effect within strata of this new, PCA-based criterion.

```{r strata_pca}
# Calculate the first principal component
suit_df$PC1 = princomp(suit_df[,c("z_t1_pain", 
                                  "z_t1_PASE_total",
                                  "z_t1_ASE_pain_avg")])$scores[,1]

# Stratify and examine ATE (mean difference due to RCT)
suit_df %>%
  mutate(tertile = ntile(PC1, 3), # Generate tertiles
         Strata = case_when(tertile == 1 ~ "Low PC1",
                            tertile == 2 ~ "Mid PC1",
                            tertile == 3 ~ "High PC1"), 
         Strata = factor(Strata, levels = c("Low PC1", "Mid PC1", "High PC1"))) %>%
  group_by(Strata, Treat) %>%  # Calculate average outcome within groups
  summarise(avg_SE = mean(Y_ASEp), .groups = "drop_last") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Treat, values_from = avg_SE) %>%
  mutate(ATE = treat - no) %>%
  select(-c(treat, no))
```

We actually see very similar differences in the stratified ATE estimates according to the first principal component, indicating that the simpler suitability metric is likely capturing much of the same information.
